<PubmedArticle><MedlineCitation Status="MEDLINE" Owner="NLM" IndexingMethod="Automated"><PMID Version="1">38184184</PMID><DateCompleted><Year>2024</Year><Month>02</Month><Day>02</Day></DateCompleted><DateRevised><Year>2026</Year><Month>06</Month><Day>16</Day></DateRevised><Article PubModel="Print-Electronic"><Journal><ISSN IssnType="Electronic">1873-7528</ISSN><JournalIssue CitedMedium="Internet"><Volume>157</Volume><PubDate><Year>2024</Year><Month>Feb</Month></PubDate></JournalIssue><Title>Neuroscience and biobehavioral reviews</Title><ISOAbbreviation>Neurosci Biobehav Rev</ISOAbbreviation></Journal><ArticleTitle>Prediction error and event segmentation in episodic memory.</ArticleTitle><Pagination><StartPage>105533</StartPage><MedlinePgn>105533</MedlinePgn></Pagination><ELocationID EIdType="doi" ValidYN="Y">10.1016/j.neubiorev.2024.105533</ELocationID><ELocationID EIdType="pii" ValidYN="Y">S0149-7634(24)00001-0</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText>Organizing the continuous flow of experiences into meaningful events is a crucial prerequisite for episodic memory. Prediction error and event segmentation both play important roles in supporting the genesis of meaningful mnemonic representations of events. We review theoretical contributions discussing the relationship between prediction error and event segmentation, as well as literature on episodic memory related to prediction error and event segmentation. We discuss the extent of overlap of mechanisms underlying memory emergence through prediction error and event segmentation, with a specific focus on attention and working memory. Finally, we identify areas in research that are currently developing and suggest future directions. We provide an overview of mechanisms underlying memory formation through predictions, violations of predictions, and event segmentation.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>Copyright &#xa9; 2024.
